item.title: Re: not an scp; ramble imminent
item.content:encoded:
Hindsight is 20/20.

There are several articles where the Foundation got involved because something seemed occult and they then found out how it was supernatural in hindsight, but really at first they didn't have anything more to go on than here.

Realistically most things the Foundation investigates would turn out to be mundane. If they waited until something was obviously supernatural before they got involved, then the supernatural would be obvious…

Do you really think the Foundation guessing right 100% of the time is more believable than the occasional false positive?

item.title: not an scp; ramble imminent
item.content:encoded:
This is a well written story, but does not make sense as an SCP article. There is no reason the Foundation would assume the beds were anomalous, unless they plan on attributing all murders to individual mind affecting anomalies. Do people not kill people in the SCP universe for awful, non anomalous reasons? Sure, there was a lot of cult talk, but are there no non anomalous cults in the SCP universe?

No vote, it's good writing and you're good at it, but the lack of a believably "anomalous" element makes it hard for me to justify to myself why I read such a spooky story (not that its your fault that i dont like getting spooked).

I'd upvote for horror value alone if the Foundation's involvement were more plausible.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
All in all I think this is the best of the 3000 entries if you can call it that. We frequently get insane entities doing insane things that lead to body horror but it's much more rare that we delve into the insanity of why something is causing this body horror.

Even by this site's standards the body horror it's self is straight up fucking nasty but still weird as hell and not just edgy. And once we actually get into it's mind it's not evil or vaguely spreading corruption like so many elditch terrors. No, It's a total fucking nutcase and more terrifyingly he thinks he's sane. All of this mutilation and pain makes perfect sense to him. His dialog also makes it very clear something is really wrong with him. So often the entire mental state of something like this is reduced to it offhandedly mentioning that it doesn't think like a human and something about squids and that's it.

Bonus points if everything is does is more evil than anything. This monster's so alien it probably doesn't even understand good and evil correctly. And on the actual things he's doing even by this site's standards the body horror it's self is straight up fucking nasty but still weird as hell and not just edgy. But you left a bunch of it really vague like the unexplained hole full of organs that helps immensely. It's truly amazing how much you were able to characterize the monster so well in such a short span of time.

item.content:encoded:
I once started work on a tale based on this idea. A few excerpts:

+ One
- Hide

Item #: PAC-21684

Provisional Object Class: Euclid

Interim Containment Procedures: [Not Yet Defined]

Description: PAC-21684 is "The Grey Towers", an Estonian daytime soap opera which no one has ever seen. It is broadcast each Monday at 14:00 on the Kanal 1 channel, each episode running for 58 minutes including advertising breaks.

Audience research has consistently failed to find anyone who recalls seeing more than several seconds of the programme. Some remember seeing it mentioned in TV listings, and a few admit to having channel surfed past it.

+ Two
- Hide

PAC - "Potential Anomalous Classification". It's what we call things that might be SCPs, before we decide whether they are or not. There's been hundreds of thousands over the years - some turn out to be hoaxes, more are urban legends, a few are the real deal…and some we just never figure out.

+ Three
- Hide

A diamond engagement ring that's been involved in 17 consecutive broken marriages. Anomaly, or sign of the times? PAC-12779, still undetermined.

An infectious but symptomless virus that's been passed among at least 103 people, every one of who eventually dies in a peanut butter related accident. Cosmic joke, or bug in the monitoring software? PAC-10074.

A recipe for root beer that when recited backwards opens a portal to a parallel world ruled by sentient sloths. The recipe is PAC-371, the portal is PAC-371-1 and the world is PAC-371-2. Except it hasn't worked since 1854, so no one's interested in resuming research.

PAC-87855. A woman who has been abducted by at least three serial killers, and each time escaped. The unluckiest woman in the world? The luckiest victim? Generator of serial killers?

PAC-44113. A pair of doors that only let white people unlock them. They used to belong to a golf club.
